title: .sylviapack manifest
description: sylviapack/manifest.json, the first entry of a .sylviapack v1 wired-transfer bundle (plan 8.5, 16.4; ADR-0010). The container is a single-volume ZIP (ZIP64 when needed) laid out back to back with no archive comment: entry 1 is this manifest (stored), entry 2 is sylviapack/manifest.sha256 (stored, exactly 65 bytes: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the manifest entry's bytes followed by a line feed), then one entry content/<path> per file in manifest order. Audio, EPUB, PDF and cover entries are stored (method 0); text and Markdown may be deflated (method 8). Entries are regular, non-executable files only. Rules the schema cannot express and readers must enforce: paths are Unicode NFC and unique after case folding and normalization, and no path is also a folder of another; total_size is the sum of size; group_id on a file names a group in groups; every audio member of an audiobook group has a unique order >= 1, and only audio and cover files belong to an audiobook group; order appears only with group_id; group_id values in groups are unique; at most 500 audio members per audiobook group; the per-kind size limits (defaults in ADR-0010: audio 20 GiB, PDF 2 GiB, EPUB 1 GiB, text and Markdown 256 MiB, cover 32 MiB), a total_size of at most 200 GiB, and the 10,000-entry limit (manifest entries included). Readers also refuse, beyond what this schema checks (ADR-0010; G0.3 report F16): a text that is not strict JSON (RFC 8259) in UTF-8 without a byte order mark; a member name given twice in one object; an unpaired surrogate escape; nesting deeper than 512 levels; an integer of more than 4300 digits; NaN or Infinity; integers outside the readers' 64-bit fields (size and total_size above 18446744073709551615, order above 9223372036854775807); a UUID not in the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form of RFC 4122; and a date-time or pattern-checked string that ends in a line feed, which RFC 3339 and ECMA-262 refuse although Python's re lets $ match before a final line feed. Readers also refuse a manifest entry of more than 16 MiB (16777216 bytes), whitespace and unknown members included, and writers must not produce one; at the 9998-file limit, Sylvia's writer's manifest with every path at 512 bytes and every media type at 128 characters, in 20 audiobook groups with their metadata at its limits, is 9356558 bytes (G0.3 review R4-02). Every string is compared code point by code point, as this schema compares them; see group_id. The manifest never contains a credential, token or device identifier.

generator.description: The program that wrote the bundle (for diagnostics only).

total_size.description: Sum of every file's size, in bytes.

path.description: Relative path under content/ in the archive: 1 to 15 components separated by '/', none empty, '.' or '..', no leading '/', no backslash, colon or control character; at most 512 UTF-8 bytes in total and 255 per component. The archive entry name is content/ followed by this path, so it has at most 16 components and 520 bytes. The 512-byte bound keeps an extracted file's full path (a container directory of about 180 to 250 bytes plus this path) below PATH_MAX (1024 bytes). The byte limits are the rule; this schema's maxLength and pattern count code points, so for non-ASCII text they admit paths over the byte limits, which writers must not produce and readers refuse (unsafe_path). Example: 'é' 100 times, '/', 'é' 100 times, '/', 'é' 100 times and '.epub' is 307 code points and 607 bytes: valid against this schema, refused by readers. Every '/' code point separates components, including one followed by a combining mark (such as U+0301) or preceded by a prepended mark (such as U+0600), and '.' and '..' are compared code point by code point. A reader whose strings compare grapheme clusters (as Swift's String does) must split and compare code points or UTF-8 bytes; otherwise it accepts '..', '/', U+0301, 'x', which the file system resolves into the parent folder (G0.3 report F18).

size.description: Uncompressed size in bytes; must equal the archive entry's sizes and the bytes produced.

order.description: 1-based member order inside an audiobook group.

group_id.description: Compared code point by code point, in groups and on files alike. A reader whose strings treat canonically equivalent text as equal (Swift's String, Set and Dictionary do) must check a file's group_id against this pattern before looking its group up: otherwise 'WALDEN_' followed by U+212A KELVIN SIGN, which the pattern refuses, finds the group 'WALDEN_K' (G0.3 review R4-01).

kind.description: audiobook: one logical audiobook of ordered audio members (plan 8.3). publication: a single EPUB, PDF, text or Markdown work with optional cover.

member_order_basis.description: How the member order was decided: embedded disc/track tags, natural file-name order, or confirmed by the user (plan 8.3).
